sources: Read-only Azure, Supabase, Heroku, and MongoDB provider checks performed 2026-09-08

findings.summary: The only retained database-recovery path is overdue and currently inaccessible because the Free-plan backup project is paused.
findings.evidence: Production Supabase is ACTIVE_HEALTHY in Sydney and currently contains 116 feelings and 4 weekly trackers. The separate Sydney backup project is INACTIVE, its SQL endpoint timed out, and its Storage hostname could not be resolved while paused. The latest durable inventory contains seven private ciphertext objects; the latest qualified full-restore backup is database/20260827T231728Z/steady-production-decommission-20260827T231728Z.steady.enc and contains 115 feelings and 3 weekly trackers. The Release contract required the first post-cutover weekly backup by 2026-09-03T05:50:46Z, so the recovery point is overdue and omits one current feeling and one current tracker. Heroku and MongoDB have already been explicitly decommissioned, making this the sole recovery system. Supabase documents that inactive Free projects can be resumed without an account upgrade within the applicable retention window. Remediation must resume the existing project, create a current authenticated-encrypted logical backup, upload only ciphertext, download and checksum it, authenticate and decrypt it, complete an empty PostgreSQL 17 restore rehearsal, remove plaintext artifacts, and record the evidence.

findings.summary: Current operational records still describe the deleted Heroku and MongoDB systems as available rollback paths.
findings.evidence: specs/backend-migration/release.json still identifies Heroku and MongoDB as the rollback source and records the backup project as ACTIVE_HEALTHY. docs/runbooks/monitoring-support.md still says decommissioning is incomplete and instructs operators to roll back to the legacy service; docs/runbooks/breach-response.md and docs/runbooks/operator-audit.md also preserve assumptions about the legacy resources. Historical cutover and rollback runbooks may remain as migration evidence, but the active Release record and operational runbooks must state that legacy rollback no longer exists and that recovery now means restoring the encrypted PostgreSQL backup into the target architecture. Stage 19's definition of done explicitly requires the removal actions, recovery properties, owners, and evidence to be recorded in the Release record.

findings.summary: The retained React client has unresolved direct and transitive dependency advisories tracked outside this backend migration.
findings.evidence: A refreshed 2026-09-08 npm audit reports 83 findings across 1,415 dependencies: 15 low, 17 moderate, 43 high, and 8 critical. Direct axios and transitive legacy build-tool packages are affected. Package severity alone does not establish runtime exploitability, and the passing browser suite, same-origin deployment, strict server validation, and separately tracked modernization work are useful context but are not remediation or a waiver. This remains visible, owned follow-up work and does not negate the backend behavioural evidence.

findings.summary: The aggregate implementation readiness validator preserves a historical failed direct-IPv6 probe even though the approved Supavisor fallback succeeded.
findings.evidence: brief.json, design.json, plan.json, and implementation.json pass structural validation, and plan.json passes readiness validation. implementation.json readiness continues to report STAGE-03.test_evidence[7].result because that evidence truthfully records a failed direct-IPv6 connectivity attempt. The same stage records the approved TLS Supavisor fallback as passing, and current production uses that tested route. Historical evidence was not rewritten merely to make the aggregate validator green.

findings.summary: Azure scale-to-zero cold-start latency remains a known and accepted Free/low-cost operating trade-off.
findings.evidence: On 2026-09-08, one cold /healthz request exceeded 30 seconds; /readyz then returned 200 and an immediate warm /healthz retry returned 200 in approximately 0.094 seconds. Production observation already documented this behavior and the owner explicitly preferred not to upgrade accounts. No minimum-replica cost change is proposed by this Review.

findings.summary: Production cutover, observation, and exact-scope legacy decommission completed under separate named approvals.
findings.evidence: Stages 17 through 19 record the approved production migration, live Auth0 browser journeys, complete reconciliation, observation, and explicit deletion authority. The final user-driven journal and weekly-tracker checks passed; no unexpected writes were recorded. Read-only provider evidence then showed Heroku not_found and zero Atlas clusters after deletion while the Azure/Supabase target remained healthy. Backup ciphertext was retained. The repository is synchronized with origin at commit a3a66bb.

findings.summary: Current frontend checks pass; current Deno suite evidence is retained because the local container daemon was unavailable for an independent rerun.
findings.evidence: On 2026-09-08 the React suite passed 5 suites and 9 tests and the production build succeeded. The current implementation evidence at the reviewed commit records all 28 Deno API tests passing, plus passing backup and legacy-security suites. An attempted independent rerun could not start because the local Docker/Colima daemon was stopped; this is an environment availability result, not a test failure. No runtime implementation changed after the recorded passing API evidence; Stage 19 removed the retired Go tree and updated migration records and dead client tooling.

acceptance_criteria_evidence.evidence: Stages 7, 8, 11, 17, and 18 prove authenticated complete feeling history, deterministic ordering, approved response mapping and timestamps, empty-array normalization, and same-user isolation in tests and the live browser journey.

Stages 7, 8, 11, 17, and 18 prove strict supported input, exactly one durable user-owned write, rejection of client-selected identity, the approved response, and successful subsequent reads in tests and production.
Stages 9 and 11 prove the approved successful no-record response {ok:true,record:null} for an absent user/week without cross-user disclosure.

Stages 4, 9, 11, 17, and 18 prove the unique user/week constraint, atomic upsert, tracker-version and timestamp semantics, concurrency behavior, and the complete live weekly-tracker journey without unintended duplicates.

Stages 6, 7, 9, 11, and 17 prove RS256 issuer, audience, expiry, and subject verification; approved missing, invalid, and mismatched credential failures; no-write denial; and cross-user RLS isolation.

Repository inventories and Vinicius Delascio's confirmation established that OpenClaw no longer exists and no active caller depended on the three machine routes. Pre-release and pre-decommission checks found no contrary caller evidence.

Stages 10, 13, 17, and 19 prove the replacement exposes none of the chat, agent, ping, or operator paths, accepts none of their shared-secret or allowlist configuration, and the retired Go handlers were ultimately removed only after explicit approval.

Stages 8, 11, 12, 17, and 18 prove retained Auth0 login, session, and logout plus feelings and weekly journeys in local, non-production, and production same-origin operation without account relinking or re-registration. The current frontend suite passes 5 suites/9 tests and its production build passes.

Stages 1, 7, 9, 10, and 11 prove the approved normalizations: empty arrays, strict request validation, structured 400/401/403/404/500 errors, pre-handler CORS rejection, deterministic ordering, and removal of the unused ping call and route.

Stages 3 through 5, 11, 14, and 17 prove Australian placement, deterministic import and reconciliation, preserved ownership and timestamps, approved normalization, repeat-import idempotency, zero unapproved discrepancies, and a downloaded, checksummed, authenticated-decrypted, empty-target PostgreSQL 17 restore rehearsal. The original migration acceptance is met; REV-FINAL-001 separately records that the ongoing weekly recovery point is now overdue.

Stages 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, and current live checks prove a private non-Data-API schema, non-BYPASSRLS runtime, forced RLS, nine policies, two-subject direct/API denial, no client privileged credentials, no operator application route, and cloud-provider-only operator access.
Stages 11, 15, 17, and 18 provide passing contract, negative-security, browser, count, and field-level reconciliation evidence with no unapproved migration discrepancy.

Stage 12 proved Azure revision reversal, pre-write rollback, post-write reconciliation into MongoDB, repeat-run idempotency, zero-discrepancy accounting, and preserved Auth0 boundaries before production. This was correctly exercised while the legacy source still existed.

At production Release proposal, the Go/Heroku implementation remained recoverable; migration and rollback owners, secret-name inventory, the Australian private encrypted-backup control, successful restore rehearsal, operator-audit and breach-response controls, monitoring, and support were documented; and every production mutation had separate explicit authority. Heroku and MongoDB were removed only later in Stage 19 under Vinicius Delascio's explicit deletion approval. REV-FINAL-001 and REV-FINAL-002 identify post-release operational drift rather than retroactively changing those release-entry facts.

approval.reason: Final post-decommission Review approval is pending. REV-FINAL-001 is an open high-severity recovery-readiness finding; REV-FINAL-002 and REV-FINAL-003 remain open medium findings. This Review recommends a bounded remediation stage that does not require an account upgrade, followed by targeted re-review.
